Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We're ready to move forward but had a few commercial asks we wanted to confirm before countersigning the Order Form attached (Draft_OrderForm_BlueSaturn.docx). High-level:

- Invoicing cadence: your draft bills quarterly in arrears. Our FP&A prefers monthly invoicing for better consumption visibility — can you accommodate monthly?
- Net terms: standard language is Net 30, but procurement is requesting Net 60 for the first two invoices while Treasury sets up our payment rails. Is Redwood open to a one-time Net 60 exception?
- Minimum commit: need a clear definition of when a commit is considered satisfied if usage is variable across regions.
- Taxes: we will withhold taxes in certain jurisdictions unless the Order Form explicitly assigns tax responsibility. Please confirm which party is responsible for VAT/GST and whether Redwood can accept a reverse-charge approach where applicable.

Attached: Draft_OrderForm_BlueSaturn.docx (commercial draft).

Mateo / Ben — attaching a redlined Order Form (BS_OrderForm_Redline_20271205.docx). High-level summary of legal changes and commercial implications: 

1) Payment cadence: Accepted monthly invoicing. Updated Section 2.1 to reflect monthly invoices issued in arrears; added a clause clarifying that monthly cadence does not change the annual pricing schedule; Finance to confirm if ACH or wire fees pass-through are required.

2) Net terms exception: Legal is comfortable with a one-time modification to extend the payment term for the first two invoices to Net 45 (compromise from 60) provided BlueSaturn executes the Order Form and provides evidence of payment setup within 60 days of the first invoice. If proof is not provided, standard Net 30 resumes. This balances cashflow risk.

3) Minimum commit definition: Proposed explicit tiers — Commit satisfied when cumulative billed usage for the tranche >= 90% of committed units across calendar quarter; shortfall results in a pro-rata invoice adjustment or future credit. Added clear schedule cross-reference to Appendix A.

4) Tax allocation: Inserted standard Redwood tax clause but added a reverse-charge paragraph accept/decline bucket: Redwood will accept reverse-charge where local law permits and when customer provides valid tax residency evidence and a signed indemnity for withholding exposures. Also requested a copy of BlueSaturn's tax certificate for jurisdictional validation.

5) Invoice routing & entity mapping: Added field to capture invoice remit-to entity; any multi-entity setups require prior notice 30 days before the first invoice.

6) Dispute & late fee: Standard net 30 late fee language retained for periods after agreed exception.

Please review the redline and confirm commercial acceptance of the Net 45 compromise and the evidence requirement for reverse-charge. If accepted, I'll finalize language and generate an updated clean Order Form + DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: BS_OrderForm_Redline_20271205.docx (redline).

-Kim
